content: Last week I attended the 2025 AI Engineer World’s Fair in San Francisco with a bunch of other founders from Seattle Foundations . There were over 20 tracks on specific topics, and I went particularly deep on Evals, learning firsthand how companies like Google, Notion, Zapier, and Vercel build and deploy evals for their AI features. While there were meaningful unique details in each talk, there was also surprising consistency on the general framework which I’m representing with this flywheel below: Beyond Vibes So what does AI feature development look like without evals? It’s really just going off vibes. You are ad-hoc in the inputs you put into it as well as how you judge the output. If you’re building a chat bot, you might riff on a few messages and get a feel for the responses from your AI bot, and after some back and forth deem it shippable. But what happens when a new model launches or when you detect an edge case where you want to tweak your prompts? What you’ll find is there are too many permutations to keep track of, particularly with a non-deterministic system, and that you’ll want to be more systematic in how you improve and evolve your feature. Little eval and Big Eval This is where Evals come into play. First thing to mention is that people use the term “evals” in two different ways. There is a broader process of evals (big E) and there is also a specific step within that process (little e). The specific step is in systematically grading the outputs of your feature. As we’ll unpack this more below but for any given output you might score it (73 out of 100) based on a weighted sum of specific output characteristics. The broader process is what I capture in the flywheel above. The heart of it is on grading outputs, but it’s also about being structured with inputs, filtering & curating production usage, and ultimately iterating quickly and systematically on the AI Feature to drive improvements. Evals: Scoring & Signals One of the more interesting talks was by Pi Labs which is founded by former Googlers, David Karam and Achint Srivastava, who both worked on search. They talked through Google’s process for assessing the quality of search results for a given query. Google essentially breaks down what a good search result is into 300 distinct signals. For example, the page speed could be a signal, how many & quality of backlinks, the quality of the writing, the page design, how directly it answers the specific query, etc. Each of these are a unique signal that could be automatically judged either by code or more recently by LLMs. Ultimately you do a weighted sum of these signals to arrive at a score for the given search result, and Google sorts its search results based on these scores. Pi Labs’ premise is that while AI features have some unique challenges (namely their non-determinism) the evaluation should work exactly the same way. For a given AI Feature you need to think deeply about what the characteristics (or signals) of a good output are and then build a way to automatically assess it as a Pass or Fail using one of two methods: Code-Based : Works best on hard measures like site speed, correct formatting - things that can be measured with code LLM as Judge : Works best on soft measures like natural language quality or style. Here you are writing a prompt for this characteristic that takes the feature output as an input. Notion, Zapier and Vercel all effectively use this same idea of decomposing an AI feature into distinct signals and summing them to arrive at score per output. A few other important points here: You might wonder how do you know if your signal scorers are any good? Here the general advice is to have a set of human expert hand-graded examples. So for “quality of writing” you would have humans with strong writing skills manually evaluate a sample of outputs. You then evaluate your automated scorer against the human assessments and tweak accordingly. Yes this is evaluating your evals 🤣 Also why Pass vs. Fail instead of scoring each signal on a scale like 1-5 for quality of writing? Mostly it comes down to forcing clearer thinking. Hamel Husain breaks this down well in this tweet: Figuring out good signals for your feature is a non-trivial exercise. Pi Labs is trying to automate this process by automatically generating signals based on your output. How do you actually build this? You could always build this custom or you could use a platform dedicated to this process. Braintrust seems to be the leader in evals as Notion, Zapier and Vercel all use them. While I’m not going to do a deep-dive on building the above, I just wanted to drop a pointer for those wondering on how to get started. Here’s Braintrust “Create scorer” form for creating a LLM-as-judge or code-based eval. Datasets: Getting Structured with your Inputs It’s also important to get more systematic with the inputs you use to test your AI feature. This is where datasets come in. Datasets are just a collection of inputs you have saved for quick reuse. Generally there are two ways of going about putting together a dataset: Curated : You handpick good inputs that represent a good breadth of what’s in-scope for this feature. You can either generate these yourself or if you have online evals (explained later) you can adopt real-life inputs from users. Some teams segment into many different curated datasets. For example you may have a “Base” dataset for basic coverage, “Edge Cases” for challenging cases, and even “Aspirational” for ones you don’t expect to pass yet but would like to pass eventually. Synthetic : Here you get help from an LLM to generate inputs. This works especially well if you have defined your signal scorers above. You can feed those signals into your prompt and ask for examples that should pass or fail on specific signals and save those as a dataset. Going Online: Filtering and Curating Production Usage The talks kept using a term I didn’t grasp at first: the difference between an offline vs. online eval. The difference is in where the inputs are coming from. With offline, this is part of your development process and you are using datasets created by your team. Online evals on the other hand means that you take some or all of your production usage of an AI feature and eval it directly. Here the users are driving the inputs. Online evals are great because they give you a heartbeat on how your feature is performing with real usage. They can help you detect regressions as well as understand the limitations of your datasets and evals. Online evals also allow you to bring in other signals, particularly around user feedback and behavior. Explicit : You may ask users to thumps-up or thumbs-down an output from your AI Feature. This is a helpful signal. For example you may see a “Thumbs Down” when your eval score on the output is high. This might be a sign that your evals are incomplete and there’s  another signal that you need to be assessing. Implicit : These are behaviors that indicate the AI feature delivered a positive experience. For example, does the user save, copy or share the output? Or maybe usage is correlated with increased retention or upgrades. Ultimately you want to be using online evals to improve your overall process. This includes finding new traces such as edge cases or aspirational cases that you want to adopt into your offline datasets, as well as evolving your evals to more accurately capture the behaviors you’re seeing with actual users. Putting it All Together: Frictionless Experimentation Okay, so if you’ve read this far, the flywheel diagram should now make more sense. There’s been two areas of focus above: Structuring your inputs and how you evaluate your outputs Evolving your inputs and evals based on real production usage The third big idea is to make it as quick and frictionless as possible to go through this flywheel. The more iterations you can make, the better the experience you can deliver for your users as you can confidently make and ship experiments. And since production usage is a key driver of this flywheel, it is truly a network effect type phenomenon where with the right process you can have your feature improve the more people use it. One of the key ideas here is to have “playgrounds” to make it quick to tweak your feature and run it against your datasets and evals. You can handle some of this directly in platforms like Braintrust where you can encapsulate the key parts of your feature, allowing you to switch model providers or tweak prompts without any code commits. Further Resources on Evals One of the resources I’m considering is Hamel Husain and Shreya Shankar’s course on “AI Evals for Engineers & PMs” . From the free content they’ve been putting out it seems to be a good primer on the bleeding-edge of AI eval best practices. Eugene Yan has also put out a number of great posts on Evals and is a good follow on X . Finally, the conference has published a number of the talks I attended. Here’s the Zapier and Vercel talks as well as a few others I missed on the Eval track: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Vqsfn9rWXR8&t=1820s

Unexpected Dust Patterns Found on Uranus Moons Confound Scientists
illustration only
Unexpected Dust Patterns Found on Uranus Moons Confound Scientists
by Clarence Oxford
Los Angeles CA (SPX) Jun 12, 2025
Scientists using NASA's Hubble Space Telescope set out to detect radiation-induced surface changes on Uranus' largest moons but uncovered a different phenomenon altogether.
The team had hypothesized that charged particles from Uranus' magnetosphere would darken the trailing hemispheres of its four major moons-Ariel, Umbriel, Titania, and Oberon-due to constant bombardment. These moons are tidally locked, meaning the same side always faces the direction of travel. Scientists expected the leading sides to be brighter.
Contrary to predictions, Hubble's ultraviolet data revealed no such darkening on the trailing sides. Instead, Titania and Oberon, the two outer moons, exhibited darker leading hemispheres. This observation contradicts earlier near-infrared data and suggests that Uranus' magnetosphere might interact with its moons far less than previously thought.
"These findings are surprising," said principal investigator Richard Cartwright of Johns Hopkins University's Applied Physics Laboratory. "Uranus is weird, so it's always been uncertain how much the magnetic field actually interacts with its satellites."
Uranus' magnetic field is tilted by 98 degrees from the ecliptic and 59 degrees from the orbital plane of its satellites, creating a uniquely complex environment. Because the planet and its magnetic field rotate faster than the moons' orbits, charged particles should consistently strike their trailing hemispheres-yet this was not observed.
The similarity in brightness on Ariel and Umbriel and the unexpected darkening on the leading sides of Titania and Oberon indicate a different process at play. Researchers now believe dust from Uranus' irregular satellites, displaced by micrometeorite impacts, migrates inward and settles on the outer moons' forward-facing sides.
This "windshield effect," where Titania and Oberon collide with dust like insects on a moving car, likely causes their leading hemispheres to appear darker and redder. These outer moons, in turn, shield Ariel and Umbriel from the dust, explaining the uniformity in their surface brightness.
"We see the same thing happening in the Saturn system and probably the Jupiter system as well," said Bryan Holler of the Space Telescope Science Institute. "This is some of the first evidence we're seeing of a similar material exchange among the Uranian satellites."
Cartwright added, "That's dust collection. I didn't even expect to get into that hypothesis, but you know, data always surprise you."
These findings suggest that Uranus' magnetosphere may be less active or its interactions with the moons more nuanced than previously believed. Further observations will be necessary to unravel these complexities.
Because Earth's atmosphere blocks ultraviolet light, only Hubble's advanced spectroscopic capabilities could detect these subtle variations. "Hubble, with its ultraviolet capabilities, is the only facility that could test our hypothesis," said Christian Soto of the Space Telescope Science Institute, who presented the results on June 10 at the American Astronomical Society meeting in Anchorage.
Future observations from NASA's James Webb Space Telescope will complement these findings and help further probe the enigmatic Uranian system.

content:
Image: Comicbook
Like every year, the 2025 Summer Game Fest had
many new and exciting offerings
. From a dozen new indie games being revealed to trailers of AAA titles dropping, the event was packed to the brim. However, there were a few announcements that came as a complete surprise to everyone.
From the nearly two dozen games featured in the show, a handful of them sounded simply too good to be true. These announcements were unexpected, and looking back now, it’s still hard to believe them even though they’re real. Having said that, here are the biggest unexpected surprises from Summer Game Fest 2025.
Code Vein 2
Image: Bandai Namco Studios
The most shocking announcement at Summer Game Fest was the return of “Anime Souls”.
Code Vein
is back with a second installment. However, what was more shocking than the announcement itself was how the sequel was changing things up.
Code Vein 2’s
trailer
featured a different art style. The anime-inspired aesthetic and character designs were there, but a lot of realism had been put into them. The world felt exponentially bigger than the first one. There was a shot in the trailer where the protagonist was riding a bike. That could indicate
Code Vein 2
is taking the series to an open world setting. A new build system for customizing weapons and skills is also coming in
Code Vein 2,
per the game’s Steam page.
Code Vein 2
feels drastically different from its predecessor. And judging from the trailer, what has changed has only been replaced by something better.
ARC Raiders
Image: Embark Studios
ARC Raiders
is an extraction shooter originally announced at The Game Awards 2021. Now, at Summer Game Fest 2025, it finally has a release date set for October 30, 2025.
ARC Raiders
follows a PvPvE model, meaning everything from the players to the environment can be hostile.
The core gameplay loop of
ARC Raiders
has you scavenging for resources on a desolate planet. This way, you are supposed to find new gear, quest items, and more. Gearing up is an essential part of preparing to fight the AI-controlled enemies called ARC, as well as other players. The surprisingly long wait is almost over now, and you can expect to be fighting ARC robots come Fall.
Marvel’s Deadpool VR
Image: Twisted Pixel
A Deadpool game was the last thing anyone had on their bingo card for Summer Game Fest 2025. It’s VR, though, and only for the Meta Quest 3 and 3S devices. As for the release,
Marvel’s Deadpool VR
will launch later this year in 2025.
Per the synopsis, Deadpool gets pulled into the Marvel metaverse. He signs a contract without reading it and then plunges into battle against many iconic villains from the Marvel Universe. But what’s most exciting about
Marvel’s Deadpool VR
is that, according to the developers, you can do a lot of wild stuff. Things like punching someone while holding a grenade and then taking your exploded-off arm and throwing it at another guy.
Deadpool VR
is uncanny as a
Deadpool adaptation
should be. A dream game for every fan of the superhero.
Resident Evil: Requiem
Image: Capcom
An update on the
Resident Evil
franchise was expected. A full trailer drop with a release date reveal? Now that left everyone speechless.
Resident Evil 9
is titled
Requiem
, and it’s coming on February 27, 2026.
The first trailer showcased a bunch of new characters, mainly hinting at
Grace Ashcroft being the new protagonist
. The ruins of Raccoon City could clearly be seen in the trailer. But it also seems like we’ll be returning there soon enough. Less than a year is left for
Resident Evil: Requiem’s
release. Given that, you might want to tune into Gamescom this year for another unexpected trailer drop.
Lies of P: Overture
Image: Neowiz
Lies of P: Overture
was going to be released in Summer 2025. But before fans could even get excited for a release date, Neowiz decided to shadowdrop the entire thing. The prequel DLC is now available, and fans can jump into parts of Krat from before the machines became corrupted.
The shadowdrop blindsided everyone, from hardcore fans of the game to reliable industry insiders. In any case,
Overture’s
release is a massive win for everybody involved. Especially considering how there aren’t many Soulslikes of the same scale coming out this year.
The post
Top 5 Most Unexpected Announcements From Summer Game Fest
appeared first on
ComicBook.com
.

Here’s Every Major RPG Coming Your Way by the End of 2025
By
Valentina Kraljik
Published on
June 11, 2025
June 11, 2025
0 Comments
Our
Editorial Policy
.
Share:
2025 is shaping up to be an exciting year for RPG fans. Whether you’re into epic fantasy adventures, sci-fi thrillers, or deep story-driven games, there’s something for everyone. From big-budget releases to indie gems, the rest of the year will be packed with titles that promise hundreds of hours of exploration, battles, and unforgettable characters. Here’s a full list of every RPG launching by the end of the year.
1. Forgotlings (June 12)
Platforms: PC, PS5, Xbox Series X, PS4, Xbox One
Forgotlings is a beautiful action-adventure game set in a magical world of lost things looking for meaning. Explore forgotten places, bring together fighting tribes, and face a mysterious danger threatening their world. Experience a unique story full of wonder and imagination.
2. Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord – War Sails (June 17)
Platforms: PC, PS5, Xbox Series X
War Sails is a single-player expansion for Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord that adds exciting naval warfare. Command ships, fight sea battles, and explore new lands. Customize your fleet, conquer settlements, and build your legend. Travel to the Northern Kingdom, home of fierce Nords, where you can trade, recruit warriors, or challenge their rule. Will you join them or take their riches?
3. Soulstone Survivors (June 17)
Platforms: PC, PS5, Xbox Series X
In this Action Roguelite, battle the Lords of the Void and their endless minions to collect Soulstones and become a god. Unlock secret spells, craft powerful weapons, choose from multiple characters, and find powerful synergies to master the power of the void.
4. Pax Dei (June 18)
Platforms: PC
Pax Dei is a large, social sandbox MMO inspired by medieval legends. Still in early development, the game will continue to grow with more content and systems. Players can explore a magical open world, build homes, and shape their own stories. Early Access runs until at least June 2025, with progress wipes expected during major updates.
5. RAIDOU Remastered: The Mystery of the Soulless Army (June 19)
Platforms: PS5, Switch, Xbox Series X, PS4, Switch 2, PC
The beloved supernatural action RPG from ATLUS is back! Play as Raidou Kuzunoha XIV, a detective and Devil Summoner, solving the mystery of the Soulless Army with help from your demons. Enjoy improved visuals, new voiceovers, updated battles, and quality of life changes for both new players and fans.
6. BitCraft Online (June 20 – Early Access)
Platforms: PC
BitCraft Online is a single-world MMORPG set in the ancient land of Starfell, featuring music by Austin Wintory and Rachel Hardy. Join others to build towns, explore beautiful biomes, trade rare goods, and care for pets.
The game offers a fully editable world where you can shape the terrain, build structures, and create your own legacy. Whether you like exploring, building, fighting monsters, or trading, BitCraft Online lets you connect with thousands of players and shape the world together.
7. Shuffle Tactics (June 24)
Platforms: PC
Shuffle Tactics is a roguelite tactical RPG inspired by classics like Final Fantasy Tactics. Defend the Kingdom of Asteria from the Glimmer Curse by building powerful decks, collecting relics, and choosing the best sidekick.
Use smart tactics and positioning in turn-based battles to defeat the corrupted enemies. Each hero has unique skills and cards you can mix and match to create strong combos. Whether you’re new or experienced, strategy and deckbuilding are key to winning and becoming a legendary hero.
8. Persona 5: The Phantom X (June 26)
Platforms: PC, Android, iOS
Persona 5: The Phantom X is a brand-new game set in the world of
Persona 5
. It takes place in Tokyo and features an original story with a new team of Phantom Thieves.
9. Bolt & Wahlington (Estimated June)
Platforms: PC
You play as Bolt, a mech pilot exploring a giant flying fortress packed with action, puzzles, and secrets. It’s a wild mix of platforming and combat where you can even mess with the game’s rules and uncover hidden meta elements. Think Metroidvania, but with a twist, you’re not just breaking walls, you’re breaking the game itself.
10. Oceanhorn: Chronos Dungeon (Q2)
Platforms: PC
Oceanhorn: Chronos Dungeon
is a dungeon-crawling adventure set 200 years after
Oceanhorn 2
, where you play as a team of four heroes exploring a mysterious underground maze. You’re searching for the Paradigm Hourglass, a powerful relic that could change history and restore a broken world. Each run through the dungeon is different, full of traps, enemies, and surprises.
11. Dungeons of Eternity (Q2)
Platforms: PC
Dungeons of Eternity
is a fast-paced VR action game where you and your friends battle through endless fantasy dungeons. You can swing swords, throw axes, shoot arrows, and cast spells, all with full VR motion. It’s all about surviving the chaos and becoming the ultimate adventurer.
12. Heroes of Might & Magic: Olden Era (Q2)
Platforms: PC
Heroes of Might and Magic: Olden Era
is the official prequel to the legendary turn-based strategy series. You can explore maps alone or with friends, fight classic battles, and try to bring peace to a chaotic land. It’s a must-play for fans who want to see where it all began.
13. Grifford Academy (July 8)
Platforms: PC
Grifford Academy
is a story-driven RPG where you explore a magical book world and shape characters through your choices. You’ll dive into strategic turn-based battles while uncovering the mysteries of Caldria. It’s all about growing up, making tough decisions, and exploring a rich fantasy world.
14. PATAPON 1+2 Replay (July 11)
Platforms: PC, Switch
Patapon
is a rhythm-based game where you lead a cute tribe by beating drums to control their moves and attacks. Each Patapon has a special role, so you need to mix and match your squad to win battles. It’s all about timing, strategy, and marching your way to victory!
15. Edens Zero (July 15)
Platforms: PC, PS5, Xbox Series X
EDENS ZERO
is a 3D action RPG based on the popular space fantasy anime by Hiro Mashima. You get to play as different characters traveling across planets, fighting strong enemies along the way. It’s a big adventure full of action and exploration in a vibrant universe.
16. Sector Unknown (July 16)
Platforms: PC
Sector Unknown
is an isometric sci-fi RPG where you start on a lonely planet and build your base from scratch. As you explore space, you’ll meet different factions—some you can team up with, others you might have to crush. It’s a deep, story-driven adventure about survival, power, and standing up to a ruthless enemy.
17. Hell Clock (July 22)
Platforms: PC
This game mixes roguelike and action RPG styles, letting you build powerful characters with tons of loot. You’ll fight your way through challenging dungeons using crazy abilities. It’s a dark fantasy adventure inspired by Brazil’s War of Canudos.
18. Wuchang: Fallen Feathers (July 24)
Platforms: PC, PS5, Xbox Series X
WUCHANG: Fallen Feathers
is a dark action RPG in the style of Souls games, set during the chaotic end of China’s Ming Dynasty. You’ll battle deadly enemies and twisted monsters while uncovering the mystery behind a strange illness. It’s all about tough combat, gritty atmosphere, and ancient legends.
19. The Necromancer’s Tale (Estimated July)
Platforms: PC
This is a dark, gothic RPG where you use an ancient spellbook to raise the dead and build your own army. You’ll deal with ghosts, go a little mad, and use secrets, blackmail, or charm to get your way. It’s all about playing the long game in the shadows, until it’s time to strike.
20. The Demons Told Me to Make This Game (Estimated July)
Platforms: PC
This game drops you into a demon-infested town as a ghost trapped in a time loop. You can’t do much on your own, so you possess people, whisper suggestions, and try to guide them through danger. It’s a creepy, clever mystery game where every choice and host matter.
21. Wander Stars (August 1)
Platforms: PC, Switch
This over-the-top anime-style turn-based RPG lets you create your own attacks by combining words, yep, the weirder the combo, the cooler the move. You’ll collect words, power up with “Pep Ups,” and chase down pieces of a cosmic map while making friends (and rivals) along the way. It’s loud, wild, and totally unique.
22. Voyagers of Nera (August 5)
Platforms: PC
Voyagers of Nera
is a chill co-op survival game set in a magical ocean full of spooky spirits and sea monsters. You and your friends can explore islands, build villages, and ride the waves together. It’s all about teamwork, creativity, and surviving a beautiful but dangerous world.
23. Hidden Pass (August 14)
Platforms: PC
In this tactical roguelite RPG, you play as a Wanderer—part adventurer, part strategist, exploring floating islands in the sky. You’ll gather a team of sky heroes, craft gadgets and robots, and dive into a world full of danger and mystery. Every run is different, and your choices shape the story as you go.
24. OFF (August 15)
Platforms: PC, Switch
OFF
is a cult-classic RPG where you play as the Batter, a serious guy on a strange mission to “purify” a bizarre, broken world. Alongside a mysterious talking cat named The Judge, you’ll fight ghostly enemies and uncover unsettling secrets. It’s weird, haunting, and finally making its way to Steam.
25. Inazuma Eleven: Victory Road (August 21)
Platforms: PC, Switch, PS4, PS5, Xbox Series X, Switch 2
Inazuma Eleven
is back with a brand-new story, new main characters, and a massive lineup of over 4,500 players to collect and train. It’s a mix of football (soccer) action and RPG-style character building, with tons of strategy and customization. You can even jump into online tournaments and play however you like.
26. Discounty (August 21)
Platforms: PC, Switch, PS5, Xbox Series X
In this quirky management game, you run a discount supermarket in a small town full of drama and secrets. You’ll design your store, make deals, and try to grow your mysterious aunt’s shady business empire. Somehow, selling cheap frozen food might just bring the town back together… maybe.
27. Quartet (August 26)
Platforms: PC, Switch, PS5, PS4
This turn-based RPG lets you dive into four different stories about train robberies, magic, and deadly airships, all connected in surprising ways. You can play the stories in any order and uncover how everything links together. It’s a mix of mystery, strategy, and adventure with a unique twist.
28. VARLET (August 27)
Platforms: PC, Switch, PS5
VARLET
is a school life RPG where you meet and help troubled classmates while discovering new sides of yourself. You’ll choose whether to be a supportive leader or a strict ruler as you navigate their struggles. It’s a story about growth, choices, and finding your own path.
29. Lost Soul Aside™ (August 29)
Platforms: PC, PS5
Lost Soul Aside™
is an action-packed adventure where you set out to rescue your younger sister and protect humanity from strange invaders from another dimension. You’ll explore amazing worlds and face intense battles. It’s a thrilling journey full of fast-paced combat and mystery.
30. Borderlands 4 (September 12)
Platforms: PC, PS5, Switch 2, Xbox Series X
Borderlands 4
is a wild looter shooter where you can team up with friends to take down crazy enemies and collect billions of weapons. You play as one of four new Vault Hunters trying to escape a dangerous hidden planet. Expect nonstop action, chaos, and loads of fun.
31. Marisa of Liartop Mountain (September 19)
Platforms: PC, Switch
Marisa of Liartop Mountain
is an adventure RPG where your choices and dice rolls shape the story. You play as Reimu, searching through a magical book to find the missing Marisa, with help from four supportive girls. It’s a fun, unpredictable journey full of surprises and teamwork.
32. Final Fantasy Tactics: The Ivalice Chronicles (September 30)
Platforms: PC, Switch, PS4, PS5, Xbox Series X, Switch 2
This classic tactical RPG is back with full voice acting, stunning updated graphics, and tons of gameplay upgrades. Fans of the genre will love the fresh yet familiar experience. It’s a perfect mix of strategy, story, and style.
33. Demonschool (Q3)
Platforms: PC, Switch, PS4, PS5, Xbox Series X
Demonschool
is a tactics RPG where moving your characters triggers their actions in battle. You play as Faye and her quirky friends, fighting strange creatures between the human and demon worlds. Along the way, you’ll also juggle life at a mysterious island university.
34. MENACE (Q3)
Platforms: PC
In this turn-based tactical RPG, you lead a strike force fighting off an alien invasion across multiple worlds. You’ll train troops, gear up tanks and mechs, and carefully plan each mission. It’s all about strategy, teamwork, and intense battles.
35. Good Heavens! (Q3)
Platforms: PC
Good Heavens!
is a goofy open-world RPG where you and your friends can craft, build, and explore as warriors, mages, or whatever you feel like. The world’s full of weird creatures, strange cultures, and wild places to discover. You can save the world, or just get tipsy in a werewolf tavern.
36. Guardians of the Wild Sky (Q3)
Platforms: PC
In this magical open-world game, you explore floating islands, build anything from homes to flying castles, and bond with powerful creatures called Guardians. You get to captain your own airship and sail across the skies solo or with friends. It’s all about adventure, crafting, and living your best sky life.
37. Multiverse Designer (Q3)
Platforms: PC
Multiverse Designer
is a powerful virtual tabletop tool that lets you build and customize 3D maps, scenes, and characters for your RPG sessions. Whether you’re into fantasy, sci-fi, horror, or anything else, you can create it here. It’s perfect for storytellers who want to bring their wildest worlds to life.
38. Away From Home (October 22)
Platforms: PC
This is a rhythm-based RPG where you battle to the beat in a colorful, pixel-art world full of quirky characters. The animation’s super lively, and the whole vibe is playful and chaotic. Basically, you’re here to crash the party, and make it awesome.
39. The Outer Worlds 2 (October 29)
Platforms: PC, Xbox Series X, PS5
The Outer Worlds 2
is the follow-up to the hit sci-fi RPG where choices, weird planets, and sharp humor rule. You’ll explore a brand-new star system with new characters, new adventures, and probably more corporate nonsense to fight. Expect wild storylines, lots of freedom, and plenty of sarcasm.
40. Dragon Quest I & II HD-2D Remake (October 30)
Platforms: PC, Xbox Series X, PS5, Switch, Switch 2
The
Dragon Quest I & II HD-2D Remake
brings two classic adventures back with a fresh, modern look. You play as the descendants of the legendary hero Erdrick, battling evil forces that return to threaten the world after peace doesn’t last. It’s a nostalgic, story-rich journey full of monsters, magic, and royal destiny.
41. Edge of Memories (Q4)
Platforms: PC, Xbox Series X, PS5
In this fantasy RPG, you play as Eline, a nomad fighting to save her world from a spreading disease called the Corrosion. It turns people into monstrous creatures, and it’s up to you and your allies to stop it. Expect intense battles, a dark setting, and a fight for survival.
42. Demeo x Dungeons & Dragons: Battlemarked (Q4)
Platforms: PC, PS5, PSVR 2
This is a classic-style fantasy RPG set in the Dungeons & Dragons world, where you build a party and dive into a big, choice-driven adventure. You’ll face turn-based battles, make tough decisions, and uncover dark secrets along the way. It’s all about strategy, storytelling, and rolling with whatever the realm throws at you.
43. Withering Realms (Q4)
Platforms: PC, Xbox Series X, PS5
In this spooky action RPG, you play as a ghost and her creepy doll protector as they explore the eerie town of Penwyll and its haunted surroundings. You’ll fight off monsters, uncover dark secrets, and wander through graveyards and decaying mansions. It’s creepy, mysterious, and full of atmospheric horror vibes.
44. Hibernaculum (Q4)
Platforms: PC
Hibernaculum is an old-school dungeon crawler with a creepy, mysterious vibe. You explore a huge, winding world full of danger, secrets, and survival challenges. It feels retro but brings in modern twists to keep things fresh and weird in the best way.
45. Zodiac Legion (Q4)
Platforms: PC
Zodiac Legion is a turn-based tactical RPG where you lead a magical knight order. You build up your base, unlock powerful astral magic, and fight against mythical creatures. It’s all about strategy and growing your team’s strength in a world full of ancient magic.
46. Not Only Nine (Q4)
Platforms: PC
In this story-driven RPG, you play as a cat’s soul traveling through the Afterlife to rescue their human. Along the way, you team up with an ancient being to fight off the deadly Reapers. It’s a heartfelt adventure full of mystery and action.
47. World of Magic: Rise of Magic (Q4)
Platforms: PC
This RPG lets you play as a wizard in a world where goblins raid villages and the rich battle for control. Some NPCs have smart AI, making the world feel alive and unpredictable. Your choices matter and can change the fate of your family and the entire realm.
48. Nivalis (Estimated 2025)
Platforms: PC
In Nivalis, you get to build your business by running restaurants and nightclubs while making friends, and maybe some enemies too. You can buy and decorate apartments, go fishing, and explore a city that reaches from the ocean all the way up to the clouds. It’s a chill game where you can even find a little romance along the way.
49. Moonlighter 2: The Endless Vault (Estimated 2025)
Platforms: PC, Xbox Series X, PS5
In this game, you juggle being a brave adventurer and a clever shop owner. Explore colorful worlds full of cool loot and tricky enemies while upgrading your weapons and gadgets. Along the way, you’ll meet and make your place in a quirky group of survivors.
50. Shape of Dreams (Estimated 2025)
Platforms: PC
Shape of Dreams mixes fast-paced roguelite action with MOBA vibes, letting you explore a dream world. You can customize your hero’s memories to build your own unique champion. Play alone or team up with friends in four-player co-op for the full experience.
51. HYKE:Northern Light(s) (Estimated 2025)
Platforms: PC, Switch, PS5
You play as Hyke, a young witch starting an exciting 2D pixel art adventure. Explore the world, fight enemies, and enjoy chill moments camping with your friends. It’s a fun mix of action and relaxing vibes.
52. Saveseeker (Estimated 2025)
Platforms: PC
In Saveseeker, you play as a time-traveling girl on a mission to save the world from her dad. The game is a turn-based RPG where you can overwrite save points to change your progress. It’s all about clever strategy and rewriting history to win.
53. Vampire: The Masquerade® – Bloodlines™ 2 (Estimated 2025)
Platforms: PC, PS5, Xbox Series X
Step into the shoes of an ancient vampire fighting for control in a tense, modern-day Seattle. Build alliances with powerful players and decide who rules the city. Your choices shape the future in this dark, action-packed adventure.
54. Hoglands (Estimated 2025)
Platforms: PC
Hoglands is a 2D side-scroller where you protect your kingdom from undead pigs. You gather resources, build defenses, and grow your army while leveling up your hero. It’s all about strategy and keeping your land safe from crazy pig attacks.
55. Titan Quest II (Estimated 2025)
Platforms: PC, PS5, Xbox Series X
In Titan Quest II, you battle Nemesis, the Goddess of Retribution, who’s messing with fate and punishing her enemies. Fight alongside gods in this action RPG inspired by Greek myths. Your goal is to take control and change the course of destiny itself.
Want to add a game to the list? Let us know in the comments below!

The best multiplayer games to play with friends 2025
List of all the top free multiplayer games to play with friends, offering great online communities, plus some fun full-price titles too.
Christian Vaz
Published:
Jun 12, 2025
Apex Legends
What are the best multiplayer games?
Intricate gameplay and glistening visuals only go so far; humans often provide the biggest surprises with schemes that transform even the most average game into an unforgettable experience you'll be talking about until the end of time.
Fast and frantic or tense and calculated, the best multiplayer games come in all shapes and sizes. Whether it's vying for control of the payload in an
FPS game
or fighting for survival in a
co-op game
with your friends, these experiences wouldn't be the same without a bunch of real people. We've curated a list of the
best PC games
with multiplayer functionality so you can go around killing, maiming, or, occasionally, helping random people on the internet.
The best multiplayer games are:
World of Tanks
Steel Hunters
Fragpunk
War Thunder
War Robots
Naraka Bladepoint
Mech Arena
Dune Awakening
Elden Ring Nightreign
Runescape Dragonwilds

World of Tanks
Even though World of Tanks was released over ten years ago, this free-to-play PvP vehicular combat game keeps growing and evolving into one of the best multiplayer PC games. With its bustling servers and international player base, you'll never struggle to find a team whenever you get that urge to hop into a tank and blow stuff up.
Whether you favor brute force battling or a more strategic approach, the easy-to-grasp game mechanics lend themselves well to different playstyles. Destroy all enemy tanks with powerful artillery fire right off the bat, or, if you'd instead take the subtle approach, you can triumph by finding a way into your opponent's base and capturing it from within.
The more you play, the more vehicles you unlock, with over 600 of the
best tanks
from around the world to discover and exclusive rewards for those who want to participate in clan battles. It's a very moreish game, which may seem straightforward at first, but the more you play, the better you'll get and the more you'll discover. With handheld play available via the World of Tanks: Blitz mobile version, there's much fun to have here. Trust us - you'll be in a world of thanks once you're hooked.
Play World of Tanks for free
.
Play for free
Steel Hunters
The greatest multiplayer experiences excel at giving you snappy, great matches that push your skills - Steel Hunters is exactly that. Each match puts you back at square one (minus some upgrades between each extraction), as you and another player tackle various enemy drones and players, pushing your skills in a variety of mechs.
Despite the stomping heaviness of enemy players, firefights can occur almost instantly, giving you a sense of tension and challenge that every multiplayer game strives to offer. If you manage to defeat enemy teams and survive to see another day, you can safely extract, taking your resources and upgrading for your future expeditions.
Play Steel Hunters for free
.
Play for free
Fragpunk
There's nothing quite like sitting down after a hectic day and playing alongside four friends or strangers in some intense 5v5 matches - and that's where Fragpunk comes in. This exhilarating FPS sees you choose one of many heroes and take on various arenas as you take turns to plant or defuse 'bombs', or you can opt for the more casual-friendly modes if you so wish. Give our
Fragpunk tier list
a read to discover who the best Lancers are in the game.
Where Fragpunk differs from rivals like Valorant and Counter-Strike 2 is the unique Shard Cards mechanic, which adds a new layer of strategy and choices in each of your matches. Some are expensive to use, while some are cheap, but each offers an intriguing ability that could help you win every match you play. Alongside the fantastic gunplay and tense maps, Fragpunk makes for a truly engaging shooter that is not only great but is also free - so you have no excuse not to give it a try. Speaking of free, our
Fragpunk codes
list rewards you with several in-game goodies like gold, sticker packs, and more.
Play Fragpunk for free
.
Play for free
War Thunder
War Thunder is a free-to-play multiplayer game all about military vehicles knocking seven bells out of one another, whether in aerial dog fights, sprawling tank battles, or naval skirmishes. That pitch might sound familiar, but no
free MMO
has achieved what War Thunder has regarding quality, balancing, and the sheer scope of vehicles waiting to be unlocked. While the multiplayer game started with a humble suite of aircraft and ground vehicles you'll recognize from
WW2 games
, its myriad tech trees now encompass the military histories - past and present - of several nations, from global superpowers to smaller nations famed for punching above their weight.
Its incredibly detailed ballistics modeling and simulation game modes separate this
war game
from its competitors. A 1v1 between two tanks can be affected by countless factors, such as armor thickness, armor angle, material, shell size and type, and distance from the target can be the difference between a shot ricocheting and dealing no damage or piercing and wiping out the entire enemy crew. The more you play, the more you learn to spot different types of vehicles so you can exploit their weak points and win the fight with a single well-placed shot. It's an endlessly satisfying loop, and with hundreds of vehicles to earn, it will be a long time before you run out of new content.
Play War Thunder for free
.
Play for Free
War Robots
Tanks and planes are one thing, but what about a giant mech with multiple rocket launchers strapped onto its chassis? War Robots might be the game for you, especially if you're looking for 6v6 multiplayer battles with a tremendous amount of customization options., especially if they're fans of mech-on-mech 6v6 skirmishes.
With over 50 robots to pick from and many different gun options, from ballistic rounds to explosive rockets, you can customize them for many different play styles, from tank-like brutes to nimble scouts picking away at the competition. With 14 maps to fight on, no match is indeed the same.
Play War Robots for free
.
